newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-MATTHAEUS FIT FOR BAYERN'S MIDWEEK CUP CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATTHAEUS FIT FOR BAYERN'S MIDWEEK CUP CLASH.

text.p: Former World Cup captain Lothar Matthaeus will be fit to play in Bayern Munich's clash with Karlsruhe in the German Cup quarter-finals on Wednesday despite hurting his thigh at the weekend.

Matthaeus had to leave the field in the first half of Bayern's 3-0 defeat of St. Pauli on Saturday when the Bundesliga resumed action after the winter break and he had been expected to be ruled out of the Cup game.
But the Bayern captain said on Monday: "Things are looking okay. It shouldn't be a problem for Wednesday."

Bayern, who hold a two-point lead over reigning champions Borussia Dortmund, are on course for the league and Cup double. After their early exit from Europe this season, the UEFA Cup holders are even more determined to get domestic success.

"Of course we want the double. This goal is in all our minds," said captain Juergen Klinsmann who returned to form with two goals against St. Pauli after a disappointing first half of the season when he was criticised for not hitting the net.
The performance went down well with chairman Franz Beckenbauer who wants to see more entertaining football from Bayern despite their position in the table.
Beckenbauer was not in Munich's Olympic stadium at the weekend because he was in South Africa but he watched the game on television.

"What pleased me was the way we won," the former World Cup-winning coach and captain said on Monday. "We needed to be critical of ourselves because we were not convincing in the first half of the season.
"A victory like this is important as a signal for the next few weeks. So were Klinsmann's two goals. Strikers need to feel right and those two goals will have improved his confidence."

VfB Stuttgart, who played some of the most entertaining football in the first half of the season, renewed their campaign with a disappointing 1-0 defeat at Schalke and are now eight points behind Bayern in fourth place.
But Beckenbauer said: "Anybody who believes that Stuttgart are out of the title race is mistaken. Last season we had a seven-point lead over Dortmund but they still won the championship.
"With the three-points-for-a-win rule a team can bounce back from many points behind with a good run of form. Nothing is decided yet."
